decisions: Direction: design doc §5 hybrid — local ghoztty-agent owns PTYs; viewer keeps a layout+sessionId manifest; agent later gains disk metadata for reboot floor. User approved 2026-07-13 ('let's try it').
v0 local transport = loopback TCP (both ends already exist: agent --listen, ghostty_remote_connection_new_tcp). Unix-socket + peercred is a hardening task AFTER the headline E2E works (T09).
session-persistence is an opt-in config flag initially (default off) so the debug app stays usable throughout.
Ring stays 2 MB default for the demo; configurable size + 16 MB default comes with T11.
Reboot recovery (agent disk persistence, RELAUNCH) comes after the upgrade demo (T12/T13) — the upgrade scenario keeps the agent alive, so it does not need disk persistence.

Future direction (user, 2026-07-16): cross-machine session RESUME. Scenario: a bunch of windows are live on machine X (reachable via relay); the user physically moves to machine Y, hits Cmd-Shift-N, sees X in the machine list, expands to see X's ACTIVE sessions, and resumes one or ALL of them 'on the local machine'. Clarified semantics: the PTYs KEEP RUNNING on X's agent (a running process can't migrate hosts) — 'resume on local machine' means local VIEWER windows on Y ATTACH to the live remote sessions on X over the relay, i.e. the SAME remote-attach mechanism as the local-persistence restore (presentRemoteWindow(sessionID:) / the relay ATTACH path), just driven from a session BROWSER instead of a saved manifest. Needs: (a) enumerate a machine's live sessions [T10 agent LIST_SESSIONS + a viewer-side RPC that can target ANY machine connection, not only the local agent], (b) chooser UI to browse + pick sessions [T16], (c) single-session attach from the browser [T17], (d) for 'resume ALL', the window/tab/split TOPOLOGY must be reachable from Y — today T05/T06 store the layout manifest ONLY in the owning viewer's local Application Support, so the agent (or account) has to own a layout blob [T18]. OPEN design Q: layout lives on the AGENT (Option A — fits the existing architecture; the agent already owns sessions + gains disk metadata in T12; the local viewer manifest becomes a cache/projection) vs SYNCED via the account/relay (Option B — needs account storage, works even when X's agent is offline). Leaning Option A. Tasks T16–T18.

For zsh/fish/elvish it returns null (their integration is env-only; forwarding argv would STRIP the `-li` login/interactive flags — the agent default is exactly right for them). For bash/nushell it splits integration.command via argIterator (ArgIteratorGeneral does the shell word-split + quote-processing nushell's `--execute 'use ghostty *'` single-token needs), dupes each arg into `alloc`, returns the array (caller frees at block exit after Remote.init dupes). Caller (Surface.init remote branch) forwards the returned argv via OPEN.argv ONLY when remote_command==null — the rewrite is the full interactive-shell invocation and must not coexist with a user command (would run the shell instead of the command); a command-pane keeps `-lic <cmd>` (bash/nushell integration for a command-running pane is out of scope). tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE of the destruction: the restore liveness probe inferred 'session alive' from GET_CWD returning a non-empty cwd. During a fast relaunch the agent still had the dead app's bridge bound, so the child cwd read failed → empty reply → EVERY session read as dead → all entries removed, though the sessions were alive in the agent's table. FIX (three layers): (1) Protocol: CWD reply gains additive `found: ?bool` — the agent sets it from `getByIdStr(session_id) != null`, i.e. TABLE PRESENCE, which is independent of whether the child/bridge cwd read succeeds. This is the real cure: existence is now answered from the store, not inferred from cwd. Older agents omit the field. (2) Client: new Connection.probeSessionTimeout → tri-state {alive,dead,unknown}: ok=true OR found=true ⇒ alive; found=false ⇒ POSITIVE dead; timeout/malformed/old-agent(found=nil) ⇒ unknown. Exported as ghostty_remote_connection_probe_session (c_int 1/0/-1) in embedded.zig + ghostty.h. (3) Swift drop policy (SessionLayoutRestore): probeSessions now returns [sessionID: .alive/.dead/.unknown]; an entry is forgotten ONLY when EVERY leaf is POSITIVELY .dead — .unknown or missing-id leaves keep the entry AND rebuild+attach it (a live session re-attaches; a truly-gone one shows its exited overlay but the layout survives to retry next launch). BONUS crash-safety: SurfaceView now stashes expectedRemoteSessionID from its creation config, and manifest sync falls back to it when the live id is unavailable (e.g. ghostty_surface_new failed) so a failed-restore sync can't blank a recorded id. Also added an @errorReturnTrace() dump on the ghostty_surface_new failure path (the 'poisoned connection' OutOfMemory) so a recurrence attributes the failing `try` — see below. COMMIT: cda38f18f. tasks.notes: 2026-07-15: done. ROOT CAUSE was NOT agent-side (the ATTACH gap-fill at server.zig:784-816 was correct) — it was a CLIENT-side registration RACE. The client uses TWO separate reader threads over TWO independent streams (connection.zig: control_thread + data_thread, `control`/`data` Streams). On ATTACH the agent frames ATTACHED on the CONTROL lane and the whole ring replay as DATA on the DATA lane. The client only calls channels.register(ch) AFTER the control-lane ATTACHED reply unblocks the caller (connection.zig:1597, attachChannelCancellable). Because the two lanes have NO cross-stream ordering, the data thread frequently ran routeInboundData for the replay DATA BEFORE register() completed → ChannelTable.pushTo found no channel → returned .unknown → bytes DROPPED (inbound_ring.zig old line 388). Microsecond race → per-pane coin-flip, exactly the 'same agent, same cycle, different panes' symptom. Fresh OPEN-new rarely bit because a new shell emits no output for ~ms; ATTACH replay dumps the ring instantly. FIX (client-only, additive): ChannelTable gained a bounded pre-registration buffer `pending: map<channel, ArrayList(u8)>`. pushTo now BUFFERS bytes for a not-yet-registered channel (new RouteResult variant `.buffered`) instead of dropping; register() FLUSHES pending[ch.id] into the ring under the SAME mutex right after map.put, so buffered (pre-register) bytes always precede live (post-register) bytes and none are lost — atomic vs. concurrent pushTo. Bounds: max_pending_bytes_per_channel=256KiB (one client ring), max_pending_channels=16 (hostile-input cap); over-cap excess dropped (old behavior); deregister/deinit free un-claimed buffers. connection.zig routeInboundData treats `.buffered` like `.unknown` (no FLOW). Since real ATTACH always sends last_byte_offset=0 (Remote.zig:264, resync_active=false), no resync-trim interaction; test_client resync path pre-registers so never buffers. This ALSO closes the same latent race for OPEN-new. COMMIT: 4337a9c23. TESTS: inbound_ring standalone 11/11 (3 new: in-order flush T06c, per-channel byte cap, channel-count cap); connection.zig 93/93 (was 90); zig build test-agent exit 0; full app build OK. LIVE E2E (fresh fixture: 2 windows / 4 panes A0/A1/B0/B1, each a unique `echo PANE=n PID=$$; while true tick` loop, agent pid 43438, shells 43441/45205/45448/45688): ran 3x kill -9 + INSTANT (0s) relaunch AND 1x graceful AppleScript quit + relaunch. EVERY cycle, ALL 4 panes replayed pre-gap scrollback (oldest replayed tick well before the pre-kill anchor), ZERO PANE= reprints (no shell restart), tick counters monotonic across the gap (76→104→130→148→175→177 no reset), agent pid + all 4 child PIDs unchanged throughout. 4/4 panes consistent on all 4 cycles = the intermittency is gone. That SPAMMED a keychain password prompt ('Ghoztty[DEBUG] wants to use com.dzearing.ghoztty.relay-account') on EVERY launch — the user hit this live and stopped me. ROOT CAUSE: the debug bundle is AD-HOC signed (TeamIdentifier not set); the login-keychain ACL for the relay-account item is a trusted-application entry keyed by the app's exact cdhash (its designated requirement is `cdhash H"..."`). Re-signing mints a NEW cdhash not in the ACL -> prompt; a plain launch of the already-authorized zig-out cdhash (4d477ee3...) is silent (that's why T07 never prompted). Under ad-hoc signing there is NO way to change the binary silently — a real Sparkle upgrade is Developer-ID signed with a STABLE DR across versions, so it doesn't prompt; we can't replicate that. FIX: the swap keeps content byte-identical (same cdhash -> zero prompts), verified by comparing reserve vs installed cdhash before the run. This is immaterial to the AC: the restore path never reads app-bundle bytes (it reads the layout manifest + the surviving agent); the full FS-swap->relaunch->re-attach path IS exercised, and the app relaunches from a physically-replaced-on-disk bundle. The app ALWAYS launches from the installed zig-out path (never a /tmp copy) to guarantee the authorized cdhash. Teardown restores zig-out from the reserve if a crash ever interrupts a swap.

2026-07-15: done — MISDIAGNOSIS. There is NO app-side graceful-quit hang. The '~45s hang' was a TEST-HARNESS ZOMBIE-REAPING ARTIFACT, and the original T08 `sample` that pointed at _terminateFromSender/setupTabGroupObservation was a sample of the ALREADY-EXITED (zombie) process showing its frozen exit-path stack. Fix is harness-only (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py); ZERO src/ or macos/ changes.

HOW I PROVED IT (per CLAUDE.md 'reproduce first'): reproduced the 45s via the harness (--quit=graceful reliably term=49.2s), then instrumented the app termination timeline with timestamped os_log/NSLog at applicationShouldTerminate, applicationWillTerminate (+before/after ipcServer.stop), windowWillClose, TerminalWindow.close, BaseTerminalController.deinit, ghostty_surface_free (Swift Task.detached), the Zig io_thread stop+join, AND a self-registered atexit handler. Timeline showed EVERYTHING completes in ~7ms: shouldTerminate→willTerminate→ipcServer.stop→all TerminalWindow.close→io_thread join DONE→atexit FIRED, all within milliseconds of the quit. The process then sat until the harness SIGKILLed it at 45s. `sample` couldn't attach (needs sudo; password-gated), so I inspected via a minimal Python repro that launches the app EXACTLY like the harness (subprocess.Popen, start_new_session, Popen handle discarded/unreaped) and, after an AppleScript quit, polled BOTH os.kill(pid,0) and `ps -o stat=`: within 0.6s ps_stat went Ss→Z (ZOMBIE) and STAYED Z for 30s+, while os.kill(pid,0) returned True the ENTIRE time; os.waitpid(pid,WNOHANG) then reaped it as (pid, 0) — conclusive. atexit fired in ms in that repro too.

ROOT CAUSE: the app exits cleanly and fast, but as a child of the Python harness it becomes a ZOMBIE (defunct) until reaped. The harness's pid_alive() used os.kill(pid,0), which reports a zombie as ALIVE until its parent waitpid()s it. graceful_quit() waits the full 45s for the pid to 'disappear', never reaps → times out → SIGKILL (no-op on a zombie) → 'hang'. (The kill -9 path never showed this because it caps wait_gone at a fixed 5s and ignores the result; graceful waited 45.) Neither pane count nor tab groups mattered — a zombie doesn't 'scale'; the earlier 'scales with pane/window count' was noise. The 'exec quits in 0.6s' comparison in T08 was measuring the true exit, not this harness's wait_gone.

FIX (scripts/e2e/session-persistence.py, harness-only): (1) pid_alive() rewritten to be zombie-aware — reap our own launched children first, then consult `ps -o state= -p PID` and treat a zombie (state starts 'Z') or a missing pid as NOT alive (a zombie has already run exit() → for 'has the app finished terminating?' it IS gone). (2) launch_app() now retains every Popen in a module list `_launched_procs`; new `_reap_children()` polls them (Popen.poll() reaps finished children) so a cleanly-exited app turns from zombie to truly-gone. (3) graceful_quit timeout 45→20s (now just a safety net; real exit is <1s) and corrected the misleading T08a comments in graceful_quit + the recovery-gap block.

(2) runListenUnix(): connect-probe stale-socket livecheck (probeUnixAlive: a successful connect ⇒ a live agent owns it ⇒ REFUSE with error.AlreadyListening rather than clobber; ECONNREFUSED/ENOENT ⇒ safe to unlink) → deleteFile stale node → makePath parent → std.net.Address.initUnix → bind under umask(0o177) so the node is created 0600 RACE-FREE (restore prev umask immediately after listen) → banner 'listening on unix:<path>' → same acceptLoop core as TCP with enforce_same_uid=true. (3) SECURITY GATE: acceptLoop gained an enforce_same_uid param; on the unix path it calls shouldServe(true, peerUid(fd), geteuid()) per accepted connection and CLOSEs + skips any peer that isn't us. peerUid() binds getpeereid(2) via an extern (cross-platform macOS LOCAL_PEERCRED / Linux SO_PEERCRED; not in Zig std) and returns null if the cred can't be read; shouldServe is a PURE decision (enforce off ⇒ always serve [TCP]; on ⇒ serve only a KNOWN uid == ours; unknown/null ⇒ REJECT — never serve a shell blind). The real LocalAgentManager path ~/.config/ghoztty/local-agent-debug/agent.sock fits. (b) did NOT fchmod the bound socket fd as belt-and-braces: on macOS fchmod of a socket returns EINVAL, which std.posix.fchmod maps to `unreachable` (PANIC) — the exact class of trap that once killed the agent via SO_NOSIGPIPE (socket_stream.zig). umask alone is sufficient AND safe (node born 0600, never briefly more permissive). std has no fchmodat either. tasks.goal: Wire session enumeration: new LIST_SESSIONS/SESSIONS frames (store already internally enumerable — tray.zig:33 pattern), and `ghoztty +sessions [--json]` against the local agent. Foundation for cross-machine attach later.

2026-07-16: done, commit 29ffb1fc6 (impl+docs) — task-file docs commit follows. WIRING (4 layers, all additive/HELLO-compatible): (1) protocol.zig — new frame types list_sessions=0x24 / sessions=0x25; payloads ListSessions{} (empty request, same-channel RPC like GET_CWD) + SessionInfo{id,alive,exit_code?,attached,activity(str),pid,title?,cwd?,argv?,created_at,last_activity} + Sessions{sessions:[]}. `activity` is a STRING on the wire (not the agent's ActivityState enum) so protocol.zig needn't import session.zig (layering: session imports protocol). Empty roster encodes `{"sessions":[]}` — NOT elided (default `&.{}` is a present empty slice) so the client distinguishes 'answered, none' from 'no reply' (asserted). (2) session.zig — Session gains `argv: ?[]u8` + setArgv() (dupe-replacing, swallows OOM = best-effort) + free in deinit; captured in server.handleOpen from open.command ?? open.shell. (3) server.zig — dispatch `.list_sessions => handleListSessions`; the handler snapshots the WHOLE by_id roster into an ArrayList of SessionInfo (borrowing session strings) and sendJson's SESSIONS on the request channel WHILE HOLDING store.mutex — safe because encode is pure in-memory (no OS I/O, unlike handleGetCwd which must unlock for queryCwd) and the store→write_mutex lock order is the SAME one bridgeData already takes under the store lock (no new deadlock). attached=s.bound, activity=@tagName(s.state). (4) connection.zig — OwnedSession/OwnedSessions (deep-copy owned, mirrors OwnedProcSnapshot) + requestSessions(timeout) (rpcCall .list_sessions→.sessions, deep-copy out of the parsed arena). CLI src/cli/sessions.zig: `+sessions [--json]` resolves ~/.config/ghoztty/local-agent[-debug]/port.json (build_config.is_debug suffix, matching LocalAgentManager.Paths), reads {port,pid,socket}, dials the agent DIRECTLY via tcp_dial.dialUnix (UDS socket) else legacy dial(TCP port) — NOT the app IPC socket, so it works with the app closed — then requestSessions, prints a human table or a JSON array (dedicated JsonRow struct, emit_null_optional_fields=true for stable keys). Registered in ghostty.zig (import+enum+description+runMain+options); helpgen auto-generates --help from the run() doc comment. CLAUDE.md gained a +sessions section.

BUG CAUGHT BY LIVE VERIFICATION (why the server unit test wasn't enough): handleControlInternal in connection.zig has an explicit switch listing which reply frame types get routed to deliverRpcReply (.opened/.attached/.cwd/.proc_snapshot/...). SESSIONS wasn't in it → the real client's control reader dropped the reply → `+sessions` timed out. The server test uses MockClient (its own frame reader), which BYPASSES handleControlInternal, so it passed while the real path hung. Fix: added `.sessions => deliverRpcReply` arm. Rebuilt; live-verified.

TESTS: 2 new server tests (enumerate two sessions — argv label captured, alive+attached true; empty roster → empty array); protocol round-trip (alive+dead rows, null elision, empty-array non-elision). zig build test-agent exit 0; connection.zig 94/94; protocol.zig 25/25; full app build OK.

KNOWN GAPS (deferred, not T10-blocking): (a) argv is NULL for a PLAIN shell session (client sends neither command nor shell → the agent resolves its own default $SHELL inside pty_child.spawnChild, not reachable from handleOpen without duplicating shell-resolution). T12 (sessions.json) captures the fully-resolved argv at spawn — the right place. (b) cwd is NULL until the client reports it (no SET_META yet; design §5 has the client push title/cwd via SET_META, and queryCwd fills on demand) — the field is present, populated when known. tasks.title: Agent policy: pinned sessions (no TTL), session cap 256, configurable ring size
tasks.goal: Persistent local sessions must never be TTL-reaped while a manifest references them; raise max_sessions 64→256; ring size via flag/env (default stays 2MB until measured; design target 16MB).
steps: OPEN gains pinned flag (additive, HELLO-compatible); reapIdle skips pinned; caps + --ring-bytes flag; tests incl. reaper behavior.
tasks.acceptance: test-agent passes; pinned session survives a fake-TTL fast-forward test; unpinned still reaped.
tasks.notes:
2026-07-16: done, commit <SHA>. THREE agent-policy changes + client wiring + observability.

(1) PINNED SESSIONS (never TTL-reaped). Wire: protocol.Open gains `pinned: bool = false` (additive; unknown-field-tolerant parser → older agents ignore it and keep TTL). session.Session gains `pinned: bool = false`; server.zig handleOpen sets `s.pinned = open.pinned` after create/setArgv. session.zig reapIdle skips pinned: `if (s.pinned) continue;` right after the existing `if (s.bound) continue;` — a pinned orphan is NEVER evicted (alive OR tombstone; only CLOSE / child-exit-then-CLOSE frees it). CLIENT WIRING (so it actually fires): termio/Remote.zig Config.pinned + backend field, threadEnter puts `.pinned = self.pinned` in the OPEN; Surface.zig sets `.pinned = rb.local_shell_integration` on the Remote.init config — reusing the EXISTING local-agent signal (`local_shell_integration` == Machine.isLocalMachine, set by Swift SurfaceView.withCValue in T04b; true for ALL local-agent panes regardless of shell-integration config or command, false for cross-machine). So every persistent local pane is pinned; cross-machine windows keep the 24h idle-TTL. ATTACH is unaffected (session was pinned at its original OPEN; restore just re-ATTACHes).

(2) max_sessions 64 → 256 (session.zig const + doc). An OPEN past the cap is still refused (handleOpen's existing TooManySessions path terminates the orphaned child).

(3) CONFIGURABLE RING SIZE. `--ring-bytes=<N>` flag (highest priority) OR `GHOSTTY_AGENT_RING_BYTES` env (fallback), default stays session.default_ring_bytes (2MB). main.zig: module-global `configured_ring_bytes` (set-once at startup, read-only after → no sync) + `ring_bytes_from_flag`; pure tested `parseRingBytes(text) ?usize` (plain byte count, trims whitespace, floor `min_ring_bytes`=64KiB, junk/empty/negative/below-floor → null). Flag parsed in parseArgs's order-independent pre-scan (like --port-file, two-token + `=` forms; invalid value → InvalidArgs with message); env fallback resolved once in main() after parseArgs when the flag didn't win. serveOne (the single funnel for stdio/TCP/relay per the module doc) passes `.ring_bytes = configured_ring_bytes` into the per-connection Server opts (which handleOpen already threads to table.create). No SessionStore/serveOne signature churn. Usage text updated.

(4) OBSERVABILITY (added so pinned is verifiable live + useful for a persistence feature): protocol.SessionInfo gains `pinned: bool = false` (additive); server LIST_SESSIONS populates `.pinned = s.pinned`; connection.OwnedSession gains pinned + requestSessions copies it; `+sessions` prints a `pinned` token (human) and `pinned` key (--json). CLAUDE.md +sessions doc updated.

TESTS (all green): zig build test-agent exit 0. NEW: session.zig 'reapIdle: pinned survives fast-forward, unpinned is reaped' (MutClock; two orphans born t=0, one pinned; at ttl-1 nothing reaped, at ttl*100 the plain one is terminated+removed and the pinned one survives untouched) + 'a bound session is never reaped regardless of pin'. protocol.zig OPEN round-trip extended (pinned defaults false, pinned=true emits `"pinned":true` + round-trips) and SESSIONS roster extended (alive row pinned=true round-trips, dead row defaults false). server.zig LIST_SESSIONS test now opens o0 with .pinned=true / o1 unpinned and asserts each roster row's pinned — verifies the full OPEN→session→SESSIONS wire. main.zig parseRingBytes test (floor boundary 65535 rejected / 65536 accepted, junk '2MB'/''/'-1' → null). GOTCHA hit: first reaper test's 'not yet idle' step used clock=ttl_ms → cutoff=0, last_activity=0, `0<=0` REAPED it (off-by-one); fixed to ttl_ms-1 (cutoff=-1 < 0).

LIVE VERIFIED: (a) --ring-bytes parsing against zig-out/bin/ghoztty-agent — good value + --version exit 0, junk 'abc' → InvalidArgs exit 1 with 'min 65536', below-floor '1000' rejected, GHOSTTY_AGENT_RING_BYTES=8388608 --version exit 0. (b) PINNED end-to-end: launched debug app --session-persistence=true, +new-window --command=ticker; `+sessions --json` showed BOTH local-agent sessions (initial shell + command pane) `"pinned": true` — proves Surface→Remote→OPEN→session→LIST_SESSIONS carries pinned for real local-agent panes. tasks.title: Dev workflow: silence the relay-account Keychain prompt on ad-hoc debug builds
tasks.goal: The user was being spammed by the login-keychain password prompt ('Ghoztty[DEBUG] wants to access ... relay-account') on every debug-app launch, and clicking 'Always Allow' did NOT stop it. Provide a real dev bypass.
tasks.acceptance: Rebuilt debug app launches with no keychain prompt; E2E still passes; release unaffected.
tasks.notes: 2026-07-16: done, commit caa49f690 (raised mid-T09c when the user hit the prompts). ROOT CAUSE: the debug bundle is ad-hoc signed (no team identity) → its login-keychain ACL trust for com.dzearing.ghoztty.relay-account is keyed to the exact cdhash, which changes on EVERY rebuild. So 'Always Allow' adds an entry for a hash that dies at the next build → the user is re-prompted forever (confirmed live: user clicked Always Allow repeatedly and was still spammed). The prompt fires from the launch-time RelayAccount.resolveToken()/keychain load in AppDelegate's restore path, independent of session-persistence. FIX: new RelayAccountKeychain.isDisabled (macos/Sources/Features/Remote/RelayAccount.swift) gates the SOLE relay-account SecItem caller — load→nil, save/delete→no-op when set, so the item is never touched and no prompt fires (app reads as signed out; relay falls back to GHOSTTY_RELAY_TOKEN). OFF by default (zero change for release / non-opted-in users). Enable: env GHOSTTY_RELAY_DISABLE=1 (dev shells; the E2E harness now sets it in its Popen launch) OR `defaults write com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug GhosttyRelayDisable -bool YES` (persists for Finder launches; the user's box HAS this set now — `defaults delete com.dzearing.ghoztty.debug GhosttyRelayDisable` to re-enable relay on the debug app for remote-window testing). VERIFIED: freshly-rebuilt (new cdhash) debug app launched relying ONLY on the UserDefault (no env) → NO SecurityAgent prompt, relay path skipped, app answered +list; E2E --cycles=1 kill = PASS with zero prompts. NOT unit-tested (isDisabled reads ProcessInfo env + UserDefaults.standard, not injectable without polluting global state) — live-verified instead. Durable knowledge in memory ghoztty-adhoc-signing-keychain-cdhash. A heavier 'make Always Allow actually stick' fix would be a STABLE self-signed code identity for the debug build (cert-based designated requirement survives rebuilds) — deferred; the opt-out solves the immediate pain.

tasks.title: Cross-machine resume: agent-owned layout blob + 'Resume all' (rebuild topology on another machine)
tasks.goal: Make 'resume ALL of machine X's sessions on Y' rebuild X's full window/tab/split TOPOLOGY on Y — not just a flat list of attached panes. Today the layout manifest (T05/T06) lives ONLY in the owning viewer's local Application Support, unreachable from another machine. Direction (decisions[] Option A): the owning viewer PUSHES an opaque per-window layout blob (topology + per-leaf session ids + ratios/titles) to the agent; the agent persists it alongside its session metadata (T12) and serves it on request. A viewer on Y pulls sessions + layout and rebuilds every window/tab/split locally via SessionLayoutRestore's tree builder, attaching each leaf to its live remote session.
steps: Protocol: SET_LAYOUT / GET_LAYOUT frames carrying an OPAQUE blob keyed by window/tab-group id (agent stays topology-agnostic — it just stores/returns bytes). Additive, HELLO-compatible.
Agent: persist the blob with session metadata (extends T12's sessions.json/disk store); reap a blob when all its referenced sessions are gone.
Viewer (owner): push the blob on layout change — reuse the T05 sync triggers so the agent copy tracks the local manifest.

Viewer (resumer): 'Resume all' in the chooser → GET_LAYOUT + LIST_SESSIONS, rebuild the SplitTree(s) via makeTreeNode with per-leaf ATTACH configs, handle dead / attached-elsewhere leaves (exited overlay, don't abort the whole rebuild).
Decide the local-vs-agent manifest relationship: local Application Support manifest becomes a cache/projection of the agent-owned blob for local-agent sessions (avoid two sources of truth).
